rubric_items.reason: Repo filter, weekdaysByDoctor, service parsing and the page column/filter are all tested; REQ-12 (S-5 AC1) has no test and S-6 AC2 is only partly covered.
Most assertions check exact ids, weekdays, totals, field errors and request URLs; the web REQ-11 test only asserts the cell is not 'No availability'.
Invalid weekday values (0, 8, sat, 1.5, -1), empty weekday, no blocks, duplicate blocks, Sunday coding and the 21st-row page boundary are covered.
Vitest+Supertest on a skippable PostgreSQL harness and jsdom+Testing Library, names start with IDs; but REQ-12 has no test named for it as the strategy requires.
No test counts or coverage stated; the artifact defers results to the verifier, which ran tests (pass) and skipped coverage.

findings.text: REQ-12 (status filter works as before, S-5 AC1: Any day + status Inactive lists exactly the Inactive doctors) has no HMS-28 test and is dropped from trace, yet Known says S-5 is covered. The strategy requires a test named for every requirement.

cites.quote: when front-desk staff choose status Inactive, then exactly the Inactive doctors are listed
REQ-12 Status filter works as before (known).
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID

findings.suggested_fix: Add an API test 'HMS-28 REQ-12: ...' that lists with status=INACTIVE and no weekday and expects exactly doctor 5; add REQ-12 (and REQ-13 from the header test) to trace.

findings.text: Known says S-3 combination with specialization is tested in both files, but the web REQ-7 test sends only department, status and search; specialization is checked only in the API file.

findings.text: The web REQ-11 test asserts only that the Inactive doctor's cell is not 'No availability', a weak assertion that would pass for any wrong weekday text.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the exact text 'Mon, Sat, Sun' for the Inactive doctor.
